**Meeting**
Special meeting of the Troy School District Board of Education, 5:30 PM, March 17, 2016, Administration Building, 4400 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098. The notice states that items do not have to be taken in the order shown and that consent agenda items, unless removed, are acted on at one time. The cover refers readers to www.troy.k12.mi.us, notes that when school is in session Board of Education meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) every Monday and Wednesday at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m., and that meetings can also be viewed online at http://vimeo.com/troyschools.

**Agenda**
1. Pledge of Allegiance
2. Public Communication
3. Business — Consideration: Policy Services Provider Lusk Albertson
4. Closed Session — Consideration: Attorney-Client Privilege
5. Adjournment

**Item 3.A. — Policy services provider**
Recommendation that the School District engage Lusk Albertson to assist in reviewing, preparing, and maintaining Board bylaws, policies, and administrative regulations. The suggested resolution, with blanks for the mover, supporter, and Yes/No tallies, resolves that the Troy Board of Education engage the services of Lusk Albertson consistent with their submitted proposal dated March 8, 2016, in the amount not to exceed $15,000; and $4,000 annually for updates; and that these amounts be approved as an expenditure of the General Fund.

**Supporting engagement letter**
Dated March 8, 2016, from Kevin T. Sutton of Lusk Albertson, PLC (KSutton@LuskAlbertson.com, direct dial (248) 988-5695), sent via email only to Mr. Rick West, Troy School District, 4400 Livernois Road, Troy, Michigan 48098, re "Lusk Albertson Policy Service - Updated." Sutton met with the Board of Education on February 2, 2016 to discuss the service; the district is asked to counter-sign and return a copy. Lusk Albertson (LA) will provide a standard set of bylaws, policies, and administrative regulations described as much more concise than the district's current version and which do not attempt to re-state the law. Standard bylaws and policies can be delivered upon engagement; the standard administrative regulations were still being completed and were anticipated to be finished by the end of that month. LA will obtain and incorporate input from the Board of Education and Administration to finalize the documents.

**Copyright and branding**
All bylaws, policies, and administrative regulations prepared by LA will be copyrighted and remain LA property even if modified with district input; the district holds LA's license to use them, which continues if the district discontinues the service or invokes the opt-out. The district agrees not to facilitate unauthorized use or sale, and the final documents will carry a visible, easily identifiable text reference reflecting LA's ownership rights, with LA consulting the district on how it is presented.

**Fees**

| Item | Amount |
| --- | --- |
| Initial set of bylaws and policies (payable upon delivery) | $5,000.00 |
| Initial set of administrative regulations (payable upon delivery) | $10,000.00 |
| Updates to bylaws and policies | $1,500.00 annually |
| Updates to administrative regulations | $2,500.00 annually |

The flat fees cover whatever time LA attorneys need to obtain input from the Board and Administration. Annual updates are billed on or about December 1st of every year, with advance notice of any price increases. The district may opt out by giving LA written notice at least 30 days before December 1st of any year.

**Item 4.A. — Closed session**
The Board must pass a resolution to go into closed session to discuss an attorney-client privilege, after which no additional business takes place other than to officially adjourn. The resolution cites the Michigan Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8 (c). A roll call vote is required; the roll lists Miletti, Philippart, Schmidt, Underwood, Edmunds, Fleming, and Hauff.
https://media.karpowitsch.org/troysd-boa.verbose:
Meeting notice and board packet for a special meeting of the Troy School District Board of Education convened at 5:30 PM on March 17, 2016 at the Administration Building, 4400 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098. The agenda cover states that the subjects to be discussed or considered, or upon which any formal action may be taken, are as listed; that items do not have to be taken in the order shown on the meeting notice; and that, unless removed from the consent agenda, items identified within the consent agenda will be acted on at one time. The masthead gives the district address as 4400 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098, telephone 248.823.4000, directs readers to www.troy.k12.mi.us, and notes that when school is in session the Board of Education meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) every Monday and Wednesday at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m., and that School Board meetings can also be viewed online at http://vimeo.com/troyschools. The agenda has five numbered items: 1. Pledge of Allegiance; 2. Public Communication; 3. Business, consisting solely of A. Consideration: Policy Services Provider Lusk Albertson; 4. Closed Session, consisting of A. Consideration: Attorney-Client Privilege; and 5. Adjournment.

Business item 3.A., tabbed 03.17.16 in the packet, carries the heading Consideration: Policies Services Provider. It recommends that the School District engage Lusk Albertson to assist in reviewing, preparing, and maintaining Board bylaws, policies, and administrative regulations as stated in the resolution that follows, and the recommended action is to accept that resolution. The suggested resolution, printed with blank lines for "Moved by," "Supported by," and for Yes and No tallies, reads that the Troy Board of Education engage the services of Lusk Albertson to assist in review, preparation and maintenance of Board bylaws, policies, and administrative regulations consistent with their submitted proposal dated March 8, 2016, in the amount not to exceed $15,000; and $4,000 annually for updates; and that these amounts be approved as an expenditure of the General Fund.

The supporting exhibit is an engagement letter dated March 8, 2016 from Kevin T. Sutton of Lusk Albertson, PLC, marked "Via Email Only," showing the email address KSutton@LuskAlbertson.com and Direct Dial No. (248) 988-5695, addressed to Mr. Rick West, Troy School District, 4400 Livernois Road, Troy, Michigan 48098, under the subject line "Re: Lusk Albertson Policy Service - Updated." The letter opens by stating that the firm is pleased the Troy School District is considering retaining Lusk Albertson School Policy Services (referred to throughout as LA) to help prepare its Board bylaws, policies, and administrative regulations, and recalls that it was Sutton's pleasure to meet with the Board of Education on February 2, 2016 to discuss the service. If the district wishes to move forward, it is asked to counter-sign where indicated and forward a copy to Sutton's attention to confirm the terms of LA's engagement for the project.

Under the heading "LA Bylaws, Policies, and Administrative Regulations," the letter provides that LA will supply the district with a standard set of bylaws, policies, and administrative regulations. As discussed with the Board, LA's standard documents are described as much more concise than the district's current version and, among other things, do not attempt to re-state the law, since the district is obligated to follow the law regardless of its policies and administrative regulations. LA can deliver the standard bylaws and policies upon engagement; the standard administrative regulations were still in the process of being completed and were anticipated to be finished by the end of that month. LA will also obtain and incorporate input from the Board of Education and Administration as necessary to finalize the district's documents.

Under "Copyrighting and Branding," the district understands and acknowledges the efforts undertaken by LA to create model bylaws, policies, and administrative regulations, as well as LA's intellectual property rights in those products, and in recognition agrees that all bylaws, policies, and administrative regulations prepared by LA will be copyrighted and will be and remain the property of LA even if the model policies are modified consistent with district input, with the district holding LA's license to use them. It is expressly understood and agreed that the district will continue to have license to use documents created under the agreement even if the district decides at some future point to discontinue its relationship with LA's School Policy Service, and that if the district invokes the opt-out provision, it shall continue to have license to maintain and use the bylaws, policies, and administrative regulations created with LA's assistance. The district agrees that it will not facilitate the unauthorized use or sale of LA's bylaws, policies, or administrative regulations, and understands and agrees that the final documents will include a visible and easily identifiable text reference reflecting LA's ownership rights; LA agrees that it will consult with the district regarding the manner in which that text reference is presented to the public.

Under "Cost," the letter sets the cost of the initial set of bylaws and policies at $5,000.00, payable upon delivery, and the cost of the initial set of administrative regulations at $10,000.00, payable upon delivery. These flat fees include whatever time it takes LA attorneys to obtain the necessary input from the Board of Education and Administration to create the final complete sets of bylaws, policies and administrative regulations. The cost of updates to bylaws and policies is stated as $1,500.00 annually, and the cost of updates to administrative regulations as $2,500.00 annually. The district will be billed for annual updates on or about December 1st of every year and will receive advance notice of any price increases. Under "Opt-Out," the district may elect to opt out of the LA Policy Service by providing LA with notice, in writing, at least 30 days before December 1st of any year. The letter closes over the signature of Kevin T. Sutton for Lusk Albertson, PLC, followed by a countersignature block for Troy School District with blanks for "By," "Its," and "Dated."

Item 4.A., also tabbed 03.17.16, is the closed session. The packet explains that the Board must pass a resolution to go into closed session to discuss an attorney-client privilege, that following passage of the resolution the Board of Education will go into closed session, and that no additional business will take place after that time other than to officially adjourn the meeting. The recommended action is to adopt the resolution, which is printed with blanks for "Moved by" and "Supported by" and provides that, as permitted in the Michigan Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8 (c), the Troy Board of Education shall go into closed session to discuss an attorney-client privilege. A roll call vote is specified, and the roll is printed as Miletti, Philippart, Schmidt, Underwood, Edmunds, Fleming, Hauff, with no votes recorded, consistent with the packet being a pre-meeting agenda rather than approved minutes. The agenda ends with item 5, Adjournment. Aside from the Lusk Albertson engagement and the closed session, no other business, personnel action, purchase, or financial report appears in the packet.

**Item 5.D, Oakland ISD budget.** Under Section 624 of the Revised School Code, as amended, the intermediate school board must submit its proposed budget no later than May 1 each year, and each constituent board must, not later than June 1, adopt a resolution expressing support or disapproval and submit objections and proposed changes. The Troy Board resolved that it had reviewed the proposed Oakland ISD budget and expressed its support, adding that "it is the responsibility of the Intermediate School District to be responsible for its own operations, including adoption of its budget" and that its support "is for the sole purpose of complying with Section 624 of the Revised School Code." The secretary or designee was directed to forward the resolution to the intermediate school board or its superintendent no later than June 1, 2016, and conflicting resolutions were rescinded; certification cites a regular meeting held May 17, 2016 noticed under the Open Meetings Act, 1976 PA 267, as amended. No ISD dollar amounts appear.

**Item 10.A, Oakland Schools Board election.** Under Public Act 419 of 2004 the Board must designate a representative to the 2016 electoral body and identify supported candidates by resolution adopted not earlier than 21 days before the election and considered at not less than one public meeting. Williams for two (2) positions on the Oakland Schools ISD Board of Education, each for a six (6) year term ending June 30, 2022, with the designated representative directed to vote for them at least on the first ballot at the June 6 election.
